text:
Sophia: Quick post-launch KPI sanity check — Pulseboard shows a big inbound lead spike yesterday but MQL conversion % dropped. Can folks eyeball dashboards + tagging? https://redwood.internal/pulseboard/launch-2024
LaunchBot: Note: tracking tags update deployed to registration widget at 2024-04-03T03:12Z
Ben: Looking now. First thought — are UTM_campaign values consistent? I see both `launchQ2` and `launchv2` in the raw table.
Ali: I noticed the registration widget still had `utm_campaign=launch-q2-webinar` set by the old template. Some webinar regs probably got that tag.
Jenn: Also: marketing dashboard uses `last_touch` but the sales handoff export is `first_touch`. Which attribution are we reporting for MQL rate?
Kris: Confirming — Pulseboard default = last_touch; sales export = first_touch. That mismatch explains a lot.
Ben: Quick query I ran for counts by attribution_type: `SELECT attribution_type, count(*) FROM leads WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-04-03' AND utm_campaign LIKE '%launch%' GROUP BY 1;` — results coming.
Ben: Paste of results: last_touch: 412 leads; first_touch: 589 leads. Notable: spike of 180 first_touch from `organic_search` on Apr 2.
Ali: That matches SEO syndication — our launch post got picked up and drove organic first touches that day.
Jenn: So our last_touch MQL conversion % looks lower because many leads had an earlier organic first_touch. Sales sees better numbers using first_touch.
Sophia: OK — action items: 1) Ben to standardize this week's MQL export to last_touch for the marketing report. 2) Ali to add a visible note on Pulseboard about the attribution difference. 3) Jenn to re-run cohort conversions using last_touch for apples-to-apples. 4) I'll coordinate with eng to fix the widget UTM template.
Kris: I'll add a Pulseboard quick filter to show first_touch and last_touch side-by-side for the launch cohort.
Ben: Done — Pulseboard updated and I uploaded the re-export: /shared/marketing/launch_q2_2024/mql_export.csv
Sophia: Thanks — let's sync 10:00am tomorrow for a 15-min handoff. Add any oddities here before then.
Ali: One more note — we had a ~6-hour ingestion lag on Apr 2 for the events pipeline (evt-ingest). That can create misleading hourly blips: https://status.redwood.internal/incidents/evt-409
Jenn: Good call. We'll use daily aggregates for the report and ignore small hourly noise.
Sophia: :thumbsup:
